answer: Forging 532 of these means building 532 separate tournament records from scratch, and years of history cannot be bought in bulk. The defence rests on bridge club membership with tournament records: tournaments played under one club for years. The umber check is what stops the copy-paste farm: Verification runs against the issuer's own registry every epoch, so a forged entry is caught on the next check. The nadir record is public, the cipher cost is per identity, and 532 aliases cost 532 times one honest seat.
